description: A bare boolean AND / OR may appear as a function argument - COUNT_IF(a OR b), IFF(x AND y, ...) - without requiring extra parentheses. Previously only comparisons parsed as function arguments and a top-level AND/OR failed. The regression half checks that BETWEEN still binds its AND to its own range rather than to a following predicate, and that AND/OR in a WHERE clause are unaffected. Converted 1:1 from functions/FunctionArgBooleanTest (now retired); its @BeforeEach vals fixture is inlined per test.

steps.sql: SELECT COUNT_IF(v = 2 OR v = 4) FROM vals
SELECT COUNT_IF(v > 1 AND v < 4) FROM vals
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM vals WHERE v BETWEEN 2 AND 4
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM vals WHERE v = 1 OR v = 5
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM vals WHERE v > 2 AND v < 4
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM vals WHERE v = 1 OR v = 3 OR v = 5
